The XLS-40 amendment on the XRP Ledger, which introduces a new standard for Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), was activated on October 30. Approved by 28 out of 35 validators (85.71%), the amendment went live yesterday.
 
Mayukha Vadari, a Senior Software Engineer at RippleX, announced the activation via X (formerly Twitter), stating: “The XRPL DID amendment goes live today! DIDs (Decentralized Identifiers) in web3 can be pretty confusing, when looking into how they work. Here’s an explainer for XLS-40 and DID on the XRPL!”
 
XRP Ledger Gets Decentralized Identifiers
 
DIDs are unique, user-owned identifiers that are not controlled by any central authority. Vadari explained, “A DID is roughly equivalent to a fingerprint in the real world. Everybody has one, and though it doesn’t really do …
articles.title: XRP Ledger DID Amendment Goes Live: Why It’s A Big Deal

articles.author: Tareq Sikder
articles.description:
HTX, a cryptocurrency trading platform, has integrated with 
TradingView. This addition introduces new cryptocurrency pairs, enabling users 
to monitor and trade a wider range of assets directly through TradingView.
HTX Expands Offerings via TradingView
The integration with TradingView allows users to access 
HTX’s offerings directly from the TradingView interface. By logging in with 
their credentials, users can access HTX’s trading panel to implement 
cryptocurrency trading strategies without leaving TradingView.
The platform claims over 47 million users globally and 
records a daily trading volume exceeding $2 billion. HTX offers more than 700 
trading pairs, spanning both spot and derivatives markets. Fees start at 0.01%, 
with discounts available to users enabling $HTX deductions, aimed at benefiting 
traders with varied experience levels.
Meanwhile, tastyFX, 
a forex broker in the United States, has integrated with TradingView, 
allowing users with a tastyFX account to trade directly on the platform, as 
reported by Finance Magantes.
This partnership provides tastyFX customers with enhanced 
features, including standard industry charts, advanced technical analysis 
tools, and market notifications. Users will also access a comprehensive 
analytical suite, a strategy tester, and the Pine Script language for custom indicators.
Established in 2013, HTX, previously known as Huobi, 
operates as an international platform for digital assets trading. The exchange 
holds licenses across various key cryptocurrency regions, including Europe, the 
Americas, Asia, and the Middle East. It provides services such as buying, 
selling, staking, and borrowing cryptocurrencies, catering to virtual asset 
enthusiasts.
 

 
This article was written by Tareq Sikder at www.financemagnates.com.
articles.title: TradingView Partners with HTX to Enhance Crypto Market Access for Traders

articles.description:
An American cryptocurrency exchange is set to enter the Singaporean market as it strengthens its presence in Asia. Singaporean regulatory authorities have given the go-signal to the Gemini crypto platform to offer its services to its Southeast Asian nation’s clients.
 
 
A New Crypto Exchange Option
 
A new exchange platform is about to enter the Singaporean cryptocurrency space after the Gemini crypto exchange platform, also known as the Gemini Trust Company LLC, got an In-Principle Approval (IPA) from the state authorities to operate as a Major Payment Institution (MPI) in the country.
 
This means that the government-run Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has responded positively to the company’s license application to offer its services to those living in Singapore.
